summary: This document defines the scope and requirements for the Security Automation and Continuous Monitoring architecture, data model and transfer protocols. The requirements are drawn from the use cases described in RFC 7632.

eli5.summary: It is a checklist of what a system must do to keep automatically watching the security health of computers on a network.

questions: how to monitor network security automatically
subtitle: Framework for automating security posture assessment and monitoring across networks.

tldr.problem: Organizations need to continuously track the security configuration and status of networked endpoints but lack standardized ways to automatically collect, express, and evaluate this posture information.
tldr.mechanism: SACM defines requirements for an architecture, information model, data model, and protocols that enable automated collection of endpoint data, comparison against security policies, and reporting of results.
tldr.outcome: Organizations can implement interoperable tools and processes to automatically monitor thousands of endpoints and detect security deviations.

today: RFC 8248 is an Informational standard defining requirements for SACM implementations. It serves as the basis for developing SACM protocols, data models, and architecture specifications to standardize enterprise security monitoring.

sections.title: Why Automated Security Monitoring
sections.content:
Modern networks contain thousands of devices with complex configurations. To defend a network effectively, organizations must know what devices exist, what software is installed on each device, how that software is configured, and whether any of it is vulnerable or misconfigured. Doing this manually is impractical.

RFC 8248 defines the scope and requirements for the Security Automation and Continuous Monitoring (SACM) architecture. It establishes what standardized data models, protocols, and component interfaces should be capable of to support scalable, automated endpoint security assessment. SACM focuses on enabling posture assessment, where posture is the security configuration and status of an endpoint relative to organizational policy.
sections.eli5: This document says what information a security monitoring system needs to collect and how it should handle that information to keep a whole network secure.

sections.title: The Assessment Workflow
sections.content:
RFC 8248 describes a workflow with six main tasks. First, Asset Classification maps endpoints and their components to asset classes so the system knows what information to collect from each type. Second, Attribute Definition specifies the exact security attributes needed from each asset, such as software versions and patch levels. Third, Policy Definition lets organizations express what values are acceptable for each attribute and which attributes should be present.

The remaining three tasks execute this policy. Information Collection gathers the actual attribute values from endpoints. Endpoint Assessment compares the gathered values against the defined policy to determine whether each endpoint is compliant. Finally, Result Reporting delivers assessment results for further action, such as vulnerability detection or network access control enforcement.
sections.eli5: The system organizes what kind of computers it needs to check, decides what to measure about them, sets rules for what is good or bad, collects the measurements, compares them to the rules, and reports what it found.

sections.title: Architecture and Component Design
sections.content:
SACM defines requirements for an architecture that supports posture information providers and consumers. Key architectural requirements include support for both centralized and decentralized (peer-to-peer) deployments, so the architecture works whether all data flows through a central server or components share data directly. The architecture must support role-based and context-based authorization so that access controls distinguish what each component can provide or consume based on its role and situation.

The architecture must also support capability negotiation, where components discover what formats, protocols, and data models other components support, and endpoint discovery to identify what devices are on the network. Time synchronization is critical so that time-based policy decisions (like "disable if not patched within 30 days") are consistent across the system.
sections.eli5: The system should work with a central server or without one, control who can see which data, let different computers tell each other what they support, find all the computers that need checking, and agree on what time it is.

sections.title: Information and Data Models
sections.content:
SACM requires a single information model that defines the abstract concepts and attributes for security posture, and data models that represent this information in concrete formats (such as XML, JSON, or other schemas). The information model must define a minimum set of mandatory attributes for interoperability but allow extensions for proprietary or specialized attributes.

Data models must support flexible queries, including wildcard searches and attribute-based queries, and must track metadata such as data origin, origination time, how the data was generated, and when it should be considered stale. The model must accommodate full updates (where a provider sends all data) and delta updates (only changed values), and support both solicited collection (when a consumer asks for data) and unsolicited publication (when new data is available without being asked).
sections.eli5: The system needs to agree on what information to collect, store it in a way that different programs can understand, let people search for it in flexible ways, remember where each fact came from, and let data be sent either when asked or as soon as it changes.

sections.title: Operations, Protocols, and Interoperability
sections.content:
SACM defines requirements for operations on data, including timestamped requests and responses, collection abstraction (where collection requests describe what data is needed without specifying how to obtain it), and attribute-based queries. Transfer protocols must be able to carry these operations, support versioning and backward compatibility negotiation, handle large messages and high message rates, and scale to very large numbers of endpoints.

All SACM components must implement data protection mechanisms for both data in transit and data at rest, including confidentiality and integrity protection. Access control must be enforceable at the data level, supporting geographic, regulatory, and federation boundaries. The requirements ensure that multiple vendors' implementations can interoperate while remaining flexible enough to be deployed in small networks and large enterprises alike.
sections.eli5: The system should ask and answer questions about endpoints with timestamps, describe what to measure without saying how, search by attributes, protect data being sent and stored, and work with networks of any size.
